  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 883 3040 4642, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there

  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 883 3040 4642, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 13, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:05 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher
  Community Services Supervisor, Cynthia Morquecho

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  DMV/DONATE LIFE MONTH PROCLAMATION

  Stefanie Hudak, One Legacy Ambassador spoke on behalf of the program and
  accepted the Proclamation.

B.  EARTHQUAKE PREPAREDNESS MONTH

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MARCH 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63787 THROUGH 63851 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $607,200.30 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040121 THROUGH
  040321; AND 63602 (VOID); AND 63744 (VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $106,202.79 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $713,403.09 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 13, 2021
 C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 23, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MARCH 22, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  2020 GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT AND 2020 HOUSING
  ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF RANCHO PALOS
  VERDES, THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, AND THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES REGARDING THE
  ADMINISTRATION AND COST SHARING FOR REVISION OF THE ENHANCED
  WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM AND REASONABLE ASSURANCE
  ANALYSIS FOR THE PENINSULA EWMP AGENCIES

Community Development / Public Works Director David Wahba together with Kathleen
McGowan of McGowan Consulting provided the report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA requested an explanation of the timing and mechanics
  of submission of the draft Enhanced Watershed Management Program (EWMP) and
  Reasonable Assurance Analysis (RAA). Ms. McGowan explained that the cities will
  have an opportunity to review prior to submission.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about the status of the Machado Lake TMDL extension
  request. Ms. McGowan noted it is looking less hopeful.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about the Torrance Project. Ms. McGowan noted the
  Torrance Project should be able to catch the stormwater runoff volume that is needed
  but mentioned that delays in the project due to grant funding could put the project a year
  or more behind schedule. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about ground water
  pollution. Ms. McGowan noted that water would no longer be infiltrated but rather
  pumped to the sanitary sewer system.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN spoke regarding a proposed federal legislation relating to
  infrastructure and asked if this were the type of project funds could be used for. City
  Manager Grammer stated that although he had no specifics on the bill, typically this type
  of allocation was intended for roadways, storm drains and sewer projects. Ms.
  McGowan noted that shelf-ready projects are best to have if a funding allocation is
  made. She added that political pressure on the local level could help to get some
  additional funding sources.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about drafting a letter with the help of Ms. McGowan
  and the cities legislative representatives to discuss the possibility of more attention
  focused on this project or similar projects. City Manager Grammer noted that this was
  an excellent idea, adding that he would work with Ms. McGowan and local
  representatives to seek guidance in possibly locating additional funding.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 13, 2021
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ TO
  APPROVE AND AUTHORIZE EXECUTION OF THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES, THE CITY
  OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, AND THE
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES (PENINSULA EWMP AGENCIES) REGARDING THE
  ADMINISTRATION AND COST SHARING FOR REVISION OF THE ENHANCED
  WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM AND REASONABLE ASSURANCE
  ANALYSIS FOR THE PENINSULA EWMP AGENCIES (MOU).

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  JOINT LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO AB 377 (RIVAS) FROM FOUR CITIES ON THE
  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA

Community Development / Public Works Director Wahba together with Kathleen McGowan
of McGowan Consulting provided the report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted some typographical errors within the letter, Ms.
  McGowan agreed to correct.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO APPROVE AND AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO CO-SIGN THE LETTER
  INCLUDED IN ATTACHMENT A ALONG WITH THE MAYORS OF RANCHO PALOS
  VERDES, PALOS VERDES ESTATES AND ROLLING HILLS WITH CORRECTIONS
  OF TYPOGRAPHICAL ERRORS AS NOTED.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  ORDINANCE NO. 733 ADOPTION OF CHAPTER 15.28 IN THE RHEMC FOR
  “FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTION”

Community Development / Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA asked if an administrative misunderstanding caused
  the need for the urgent basis of the ordinance. Director Wahba confirmed this to be the
  case noting confusion by FEMA staff about the need for adoption of a resolution as
  opposed to an ordinance.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ TO
  ADOPT OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, ADDING CHAPTER 15.28 (FLOOD
  DAMAGE PROTECTION) TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired regarding previous flooding issues in the area of
  Dapplegray and the golf course, Director Wahba noted that the trail running parallel to
  Dapplegray Lane had some previous flooding issues which have been addressed
  through regular monitoring. He suggested a couple options as a permanent fix, one
  option would be to create an inlet placed at the lowest point, routed under the golf
  course, and tied into their system, a second option might be to dissipate the water flow
  onto the golf course while avoiding mud accumulation.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN suggested hazard mitigation grant funding as a possible
  funding source for such a project in the future.

  MAYOR PRO TEM noted that a problematic area of flooding at June’s Trail into Palos
  Verdes Drive East had been resolved a few years ago.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 13, 2021
 D.  ORDINANCE NO. 734 AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 8.12 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO PUBLIC
  NUISANCES

City Attorney Don Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired regarding the appeal process of the determination of
  the Hearing Officer. City Attorney Davis stated as proposed, findings would be binding,
  and the only option would be court, noting that issues that make their way to a Hearing
  Officer would be considered very clear violations after staff provides courtesy violations
  as well as opportunities to correct the violation after a lengthy process.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired if the Hearing Officer cost is potentially
  recoverable. City Attorney Davis confirmed that to be accurate.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ TO APPROVE THE INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING
  AND RESTATING CHAPTER 8.12 (PUBLIC NUISANCES) OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE AND MAKING CONFORMING AMENDMENTS TO
  CHAPTER 1.24, AND SET THE DATE OF APRIL 27 TO RETURN FOR ADOPTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  REQUEST TO AWARD A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO FS CONTRACTORS
  INC. FOR THE JOHN AND LYNN TABER GROVE PROJECT

Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ inquired regarding possible concern over the cost
  variants among the bids. Assistant City Manager Davis noted that staff did have
  concerns and added that the reference check for the contractor went well.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted she was pleased to see this project moving
  forward.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN questioned the inspection process during construction.
  Director Wahba stated that City staff will oversee the project along with some
  supervision by Willdan staff.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO

  1. ACCEPT THE BID FROM FS CONTRACTORS, INC. IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $54,900, PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY ($5,490)
  FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $57,645;
  2. APPROVE THE PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT BETWEEN THE
  CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND FS CONTRACTORS,
  INC, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY;
  AND,
  3. AUTHORIZE A FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 BUDGET ADJUSTMENT
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $15,000 FROM PARK FACILITIES FEES
  AS A CITY CONTRIBUTION TOWARD THE PROJECT.

  APPROVED AS FOLLOWS:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 13, 2021
 B.  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO CONTRACT FOR RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL
  SOLID WASTE, RECYCLABLE MATERIALS AND ORGANIC WASTE COLLECTION
  SERVICES AND SIDE LETTER AGREEMENT WITH WASTE MANAGEMENT

Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN thanked COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ for her
  efforts on this item, additionally he thanked Assistant City Manager Davis, City staff
  and Waste Management for their good work on this agreement, noting this is an overall
  win-win for the residents of RHE.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that as Chair of the Equestrian Committee, she
  wished to share that the response from the committee has been very positive adding
  that they are grateful for the cost sharing efforts which will help defer some of the
  major increase, she too thanked staff and all those instrumental in the amendment
  negotiations.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA commended the work of COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ and MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noting terrific results. She inquired
  as to whom the responsible party was for the purchase and distribution of the food
  waste pails.

  Sharon Shapiro of Waste Management added that Waste Management will be
  responsible for the purchase through their own vendors and will invoice the City,
  adding that pails will be delivered to customers in late June.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted this being a good example of collaboration and
  successful negotiations; she thanked staff for their innovative and problem-solving
  approach.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired on odor as well as on the use of biodegradable bags,
  he asked if they were permissible to put food in prior to placing into the food waste
  pails. Ms. Shapiro of Waste Management stated they were not permissible due to the
  fact that they as not biodegradable, she suggested using a brown paper sac or
  newspaper to wrap food scraps.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO

  1.  APPROVE AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE COLLECTION SERVICES
  CONTRACT FOR THE PROVISION OF RESIDENTIAL AND
  COMMERCIAL SOLID WASTE, RECYCLABLE MATERIALS AND
  GREEN WASTE COLLECTION SERVICES BETWEEN THE CITY AND
  WASTE MANAGEMENT;
  2.  APPROVE THE SIDE LETTER AGREEMENT WITH WASTE
  MANAGEMENT; AND
  3.  AUTHORIZE A BUDGET ADJUSTMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $20,000 FOR THE PURCHASE AND/OR
  REIMBURSEMENT OF RESIDENTIAL FOOD WASTE PAILS AND ALL
  MARKETING MATERIALS UTILIZING AB 939 FEE FUNDS FOR THE
  IMPLEMENTATION OF ORGANIC WASTE SERVICE AND $10,000 IN
  FY 2020-21 FOR PAYMENT TO WASTE MANAGEMENT FROM THE
  CITY’S GENERAL FUND.

City Council Reports

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
recently held its Legislative Briefing; she noted that Congresswoman Maxine Waters stated the
current atmosphere in the U.S. Capitol remains polarized.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported that the Clean Power Alliance is in the rate-setting process
and noted difficulties faced this year due to the rising cost of power. He noted the previous cost
of approximately $40.00 per kilowatt hour has risen to over $100.00 per kilowatt hour. He added
that these increases must be absorbed by way of rate increases through the three classes of
power that people buy. Additionally, he noted increases expected from Southern California
Edison for transmission and delivery costs. Final decision is expected in May with the price
increase due to take effect in July.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, noted he recently attended the California Contract Cities
Association meeting and spoke regarding their continuous work on housing legislation,
specifically noting AB1372 which mandates local jurisdictions provide multiple services to
homeless individuals upon demand and the right for them to sue if they are not satisfied with
the outcome of services. He noted concern over this bill for taking the burden off the County
and placing it at the local level.
